scope: Accept sampled motion feedback in the supplied sparse scenario only. This does not certify continuous smoothness, touch response, dense combat readability, or overall visual parity.

hitFlash.evidence: Both profiles show the player becoming a clear white silhouette at 0.1 and 0.2 seconds, returning to normal by 0.4. Hull drops from 35% to 27% and the return prompt appears.

impactRecognition.evidence: The small orange hit at 0.1–0.2 seconds is visibly distinct from the larger irregular yellow-orange fireball at 1 second. By 1.5 seconds the large fireball has become smoke and scattered sparks, and no fire remains at 2 or 3 seconds.
impactRecognition.weakness: Sparse samples cannot establish the exact onset or disappearance transitions.

smokeFading.evidence: A curved trail follows the turning aircraft at 1.5 seconds; older portions become thinner and less opaque in later samples. Fire does not persist as an opaque disk.
smokeFading.weakness: Dark mottled water competes with gray smoke, particularly in fallback. Some trail granularity remains.

wakeContinuity.evidence: Carrier and escort wakes remain attached to sterns as ships cross the frame; no sampled detached wake or abrupt gap is visible.
wakeContinuity.weakness: Repeated soft puffs still look synthetic and lack convincing narrow-to-wide foam breakup.

cameraMotion.evidence: After initial catch-up, the player stays near the middle while the carrier moves toward the upper edge and the escort crosses below/right. The turn reads coherently.
cameraMotion.weakness: The initial catch-up is conspicuous. Sparse stills cannot certify freedom from jitter or continuous camera smoothness.

controlVisibility.evidence: Hull, gun heat, mission text, minimap, Bomb and Fire remain fixed and legible. Heat rises during firing and falls afterward.
controlVisibility.weakness: A ship passes beneath Bomb at 3 seconds, and a wingman label approaches the map. Touch steering and actual button response are not demonstrated.

altitude.evidence: Aircraft silhouettes and offset shadows give some separation over deck and ocean.
altitude.weakness: Dark water masks aircraft shadows more than the deck does. Player crossing the carrier at 0.4–0.6 seconds still reduces silhouette separation.

regressionsAndLimits: Irregular dark water improves white-flash and pale-aircraft contrast, but increases competition with smoke and dark shadows.
Carrier/player overlap remains a readability weakness; this sequence contains too few actors to validate the dense swarm case.
Water detail is substantially denser than ship surface detail, creating a material-style mismatch.
No comparison to actual phone FPS was made.
priorities: Reduce local water contrast under smoke/shadows or strengthen their controlled separation without adding broad glow.
Replace repeated wake puffs with a continuous tapered foam structure and irregular edge breakup.
Keep player silhouette distinguishable over the tan carrier deck and in crowded combat.
